Hong Kong Developers Fair P/E Assumption The rationale for changing the fair P/E assumption to 10 from 12 is based on the following: The long-term average P/E for Hong Kong developers has been 10; Hong Kong developers are likely to experience more competition in the future as they invest in opportunities outside of Hong Kong, and Hong Kong residential property values present downside risk from here; Earnings for developers are expected to be more volatile in nature compared to REITs as earnings are more linked to the rising and falling fortunes of the (residential) property market cycle; From an ESG perspective, Hong Kong developers score poorly from a social perspective (high housing prices due to tight supply leads to housing affordability/social inequality issues), and also from a corporate governance perspective (as illustrated by the family feud-driven boardroom changes experienced by index heavyweight Sun Hung Kai Properties over the period from 2008 to 2016).

extracted_context.summary_text: US SMID Conviction Update April 2025 CMA Team Executive Summary Executive Table Executive Summary US Small Caps have different key sector drivers than large caps, with Financial Services, Industrials and Consumer Cyclicals accounting for the majority. They also have lower international revenue exposure and less concentration. We find sector exposure can explain a large proportion of the returns of US Small Caps. However, there has been a divergence YTD, suggesting a more idiosyncratic driver over this shorter period, which we find is coming from sentiment rather than fundamentals. In terms of fundamentals, we find the absolute levels of profitability are lower. Growth, on the other hand is higher and this is what drives the higher PE. We find US Small Caps are more sensitive to macroeconomic variables compared to Large Caps. While we find no evidence of an unconditional small cap premium, we see strong evidence that buying at attractive valuation levels will lead to high forward returns. slide_titles: Korea is moderately unattractive from an asset class level perspective, while it is fairly valued from an MER perspectiv
Korean Equity Market is Heavily Weighted in the Technology Sector, with Heavy Stock Concentration
extracted_context.summary_text: Multi Asset Research Asia Equity Research MIM EMEA Korea Conviction Update September 2025 Korea is moderately unattractive from an asset class level perspective, while it is fairly valued from an MER perspective, leading to an overall score of Medium. Korea is heavily weighted in the Technology Sector, and has extremely large stock concentration, greater even than the US and UK, with the top 10 stocks making up almost 60% of the index, and Samsung alone represent close to 30%. When considering macro or country economic news (such as corporate governance) it is worth noting the stock specific nature of the index may drive returns more than these aggregate events. Korean returns and fundamentals are also becoming more idiosyncratic relative to global fundamentals. Related to the above, we find that the returns are not well explained by their sector exposure. We also find Korean returns and fundamentals are becoming more idiosyncratic relative to global markets. Large stock specific risk that Samsung loses market share given the rapid increase in Chinese memory expertise. Corporate governance reforms in July 2025 to increase shareholder rights increased market optimism. However, it is still too early too see if this will lead to any real positive improvement, and we further estimate that the upside from corporate governance to be in the region of c.1% expected returns. In terms of potential portfolio considerations, we find cash flows are more sensitive relative to global equities than most DM’s, increasing cyclicality risk. Relative Valuation Medium-High High Brazil’s relative valuation score falls one notch to medium-high. While Brazil is not as overvalued as other equity asset classes, it is not a screaming buy either. Fundamental Risks Low-Medium Low-Medium Fundamental risk remains at low-medium, though the overall risk outlook has deteriorated. We have elected to account for this heightened risk though an increased cost of equity in our VIR model. Central Bank Credibility Remains a Concern
extracted_context.summary_text: Turkey Inflation Refresh March 2019 Impact of Using Consensus Inflation on Turkey Inflation Assumptions The impact of using 2 years of consensus inflation is meaningful for Turkey’s long term average inflation In effect, the 10 year average of 10% is now obtained using a long term estimate of around 8.5%-9.0% The somewhat changes the scope of the estimate and allows us to focus more on what type of number we truly think can be achieved over the long run Turkey CPI Weights 3 Source: Turkish Statistical Institute Historical Success Analysis of Different Regimes Average CPI Median CPI Average Deviation from Target Median Deviation from Target Implicit Inflation Targeting 2002-2005 23.4 17.3 4.6 2.2 Inflation Targeting 2006-2018 9.1 8.7 3.9 3.7 Post GFC Policy-Integrating Financial Stability 2011-2018 9.3 8.5 4.3 3.5 Erdogan Era 7/2014-2018 10.5 9.2 5.5 4.2 Inflation Targeting ex 2017/18 2006-2016 8.3 8.2 3.0 3.1 Post GFC Policy ex 2017/18 2011-2017 7.9 7.8 2.8 2.8 Erdogan Era ex 2017/2018 7/2014-2016 8.0 7.9 3.0 2.9 Central Bank Credibility Remains a Concern It is important to note that while central bank credibility has been an issue for a while in Turkey, the expanded powers given to the executive in 2018 further damaged the ability of the CB to be an independent arm In 2018, President Erdogan claimed the exclusive power to appoint central bank rate-setters and named his son-in-law as overseer of economic policy. This follows several years of departures from his investor friendly team. As part of his election in 2018 that expanded his powers, he promised to take more control over monetary policy. He has repeatedly stated that he believes that keeping borrowing costs low is a priority and that higher rates actually lead to higher inflation. While the central bank did raise rates aggressively in September, 2018 (from 17.75 to 24), Erdogan was critical of the move and let the world know that his patience with these types of moves was limited. Many believe that the current move towards relative orthodoxy is a temporary one.

Key points 3 Chinese banks have not been immune to poor lending. Government helped tidy up the mess in the late 1990s/ 2000s. The Chinese government is well aware that it needs to reduce the risks building up in the domestic financial system. Following the GFC, government initiated a stimulus package, with formal bank credit used as the distribution mechanism. Alongside the formal bank loans, money from the informal sector was funnelled through financial institutions. Under pressure from multiple factors at home and abroad, the risks are multiple, broad, hidden, complex, sudden, contagious, and hazardous. The structural unbalance is salient; law-breaking and disorders are rampant; latent risks are accumulating; [and the financial system’s] vulnerability is obviously increasing. [China] should prevent both the “black swan” events and the “gray rhino” risks.” Government will look to tighten liquidity, encouraging more market determined credit allocation and remove the protection that inefficient SOEs enjoy.
